paragraphs.text: Venice has long struggled with mass tourism. Before the pandemic, the city of around 50,000 residents received more than 20 million visitors a year, many of them day-trippers who spent little money locally. In 2021, large cruise ships were banned from entering the lagoon near the city centre, and in 2024 Venice became the first city in the world to charge day visitors an entry fee on busy days. Officials say the aim is not to raise money but to manage numbers, although critics argue that a fee of five euros is too low to discourage anyone.
